audit.whatIsWrong: Four separate places say Sylas "steals Abyssal Voyage" with his ultimate. Hijack steals the target's ULTIMATE. Tahm Kench's ultimate is Devour. Abyssal Voyage is not in his kit at all — his W is Abyssal Dive — so the claim is wrong about both the ability name and which slot Hijack takes.
audit.why: The whole level-6 section is built on this: 'the global pressure you planned to exert is now a tool he can point right back at your team'. Tahm Kench has no global pressure to exert and Sylas cannot take his W. A player reads this and plays level 6 defensively for a threat that does not exist.
audit.corrected: Hijack (80/55/30s, held up to 90s) copies Devour. Crucially Sylas does not inherit An Acquired Taste — his own basic attacks apply the stacks, so he must land three autos on a target before the stolen Devour will fire.
sources: League Wiki — Sylas: Hijack (Tahm Kench interaction)

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect: the entry never names a single Sylas ability — everything is "his E chain-dash", "W drain", "his R".
audit.why: The names carry the numbers. Abscond/Abduct is 13/12/11/10/9s with a 3.5-second recast window; Chain Lash is 10/9/8/7/6s and its intersection detonates after a 0.6s delay; Kingslayer is 12/10.5/9/7.5/6s; Petricite Burst gives him an empowered auto after every cast. None of that is usable while the abilities are anonymous.
audit.corrected: Petricite Burst (P), Chain Lash (Q), Kingslayer (W), Abscond/Abduct (E), Hijack (R) — named with their cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.you[1] says to pre-activate Thick Skin's shield "to absorb his W drain burst and deny his healing window", and whys[5] says his AP item makes "sustained swallow windows heal him back to near-full while you hold him in Devour".
audit.why: Kingslayer heals Sylas based on his own missing health (scaling to 100% of the heal), not on the damage he lands on you — so shielding it changes nothing about the heal. And Devour is a suppression: a suppressed Sylas cannot cast Kingslayer at all, so he cannot be healing himself while you are holding him.
audit.corrected: Kingslayer's heal scales with Sylas's missing health, which means a chunked-but-alive Sylas heals hardest. While Devour has him suppressed he cannot cast anything.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[3] is labelled "Lvl 2-3" and says "Your 3-stack Tongue Lash stun into Devour is live". Devour is the ultimate; it is not available until level 6.
audit.why: It promises a combo the player cannot cast for another three or four levels, which is exactly the kind of thing that gets someone killed walking into an all-in they cannot finish.
audit.corrected: At 2-3 the 3-stack stun is the whole punish — stun into autos. Devour joins it at 6.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart gives Sylas Level 6 on the strength of the false 'he steals your global' claim, in a lane Tahm Kench wins 51.02% over 1762 games.
audit.why: Once the stolen-ultimate premise is corrected, there is no reason level 6 belongs to Sylas — he has to build his own An Acquired Taste stacks before the stolen Devour does anything, while Tahm Kench's own Devour is immediately live against a champion who commits with a 400-range dash.
audit.corrected: Level 6 becomes Skill rather than Sylas.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing mentions Petricite Burst, so the trade pattern reads as pure ability poke.
audit.why: Every ability Sylas casts loads an empowered basic attack for 4 seconds. The real trade shape is cast-then-auto, which is why he wins short exchanges he appears to have spent his mana on.
audit.corrected: Expect an empowered auto after every Sylas cast — that trailing attack is where the trade damage actually comes from.

edits.before: From levels 4 through 5 this lane is a genuine skill contest — you are fishing for clean 3-stack setups and he is hunting for E angles where your Q is already thrown. Play the wave; freeze near your tower if ahead, and let his E dash bring him to you where you can wall him off with Q first. Level 6 is where the matchup tips his way: Sylas immediately steals Abyssal Voyage, which means the global pressure you planned to exert is now a tool he can point right back at your team. Do not telegraph the R pool for a long-range play unless you are certain he cannot steal it and arrive first — he often beats you to the destination because his kit has more raw damage to finish fights. Play Rift around his R cooldown.
edits.after: From levels 4 through 5 this lane is a genuine skill contest — you are fishing for clean 3-stack setups and he is hunting for Abscond angles where your Q is already thrown. Play the wave; freeze near your tower if ahead, and let his dash bring him to you where you can wall him off with Q first. Remember the Abduct recast expires 3.5 seconds after the dash — survive that and the stun is gone for another 9-13. Level 6 is less his than it looks: Hijack copies Devour, but Sylas does not inherit An Acquired Taste, so he has to land three of his own basic attacks on a target before the stolen ult fires. Your Devour has no such delay. Play around his Hijack cooldown of 80/55/30.

notes: The packet's suspectNames hit on wants.you[0] ("Stack An Acquired Taste") is a false positive — that is the correct passive name. The real name errors here were the four "steals Abyssal Voyage" lines, which the detector missed entirely because it only looks for near-misses. Champion-wide: "Abyssal Voyage" appears 182 times across champ-data/content/tahmkench.js and is Tahm Kench's pre-rework ultimate; his current W is Abyssal Dive and he has no global ability. No WKM_LINES issues seen.
